text.title: New Dependency Risk Checklist Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Is the package already present in the committed lockfile (directly or transitively) at the same major version?

branch.conclusion: Skip: no new supply-chain surface is added. Import from the existing version; a major-version bump is handled by the named upgrade owner, not by a new record.

branch.question: Does the package metadata declare an SPDX licence that is permissive, or copyleft but already approved for this distribution model?

branch.conclusion: Stop. Resolve the licence from metadata and the LICENSE file; if copyleft and the distribution model is not approved for it, reject and record the replacement under `alternative`.

branch.question: Does the OSV.dev / GitHub Advisory lookup for the exact version return an open, unpatched advisory?

branch.conclusion: Decision is `reject` or `accept-with-mitigation` naming the advisory id and the mitigation; the dated lookup URL goes into `evidence[]`.

branch.question: Does the registry show more than one maintainer AND a release inside the last 12 months, with no install-time scripts and a `repository` field matching the README?

branch.conclusion: Approve only with a named fallback (vendor, fork, alternative) written into `decision`; otherwise reject.
Read the install script and verify the repository link before anything else; typosquat or remote-binary hook is a reject.
Run the full record: transitive count, alternative including in-house, exact version plus lockfile commit, upgrade owner and patch window.

example.p: `dayjs@1.11.10` is not in the lockfile; licence is MIT; OSV lookup clean; 3 maintainers, release 2 months ago, no install scripts, repository matches. Healthy branch → run-the-checklist: `transitive_count: 0`, `alternative: in-house (rejected: locale tables), already-in-tree: none`, owner `swe:alice`, `patch_window: 7d`.
